gaps.title: Core-only native chat, especially remote
gaps.issue: Private fixtures prove local Core-owned adapter permission and detach/reconnect contracts, including shipped signed helper bytes. Desktop conversion/reboot recovery is removed; native GUI/real-agent lifecycle is untested. Installed Core 0.1.19 schema machine.exec is batch-only; pinned 0.1.18 source has no supported arbitrary duplex route to the existing adapter connector. A chat-named RPC is not inherently required. See evidence/t06-core-duplex-route-audit.md.
gaps.required_evidence: Herdr-owned endpoint discovery and stable machine/terminal identity with an authenticated non-PTY lossless duplex route to the installed adapter connector; bounded backpressure, EOF/cancel/disconnect/exit/lifetime guarantees, permission semantics and local/remote native scenarios A14–A16/A54. A generic supported streaming facility could suffice.
gaps.forbidden_workaround: A new Spaceport SSH relay, mobile server, automatic agent conversion/resume or claiming terminal fallback equals native chat.

gaps.title: Core-mediated loopback service forwarding
gaps.issue: Retained forwarding requirement has no dedicated method in the inspected Core method table.
gaps.required_evidence: Documented supported route with owner/lifetime and an end-to-end loopback-service test A27.
gaps.forbidden_workaround: Parallel host manager, public service rebinding or silently configuring Tailscale Serve.

gaps.title: General binary transfer parity
gaps.issue: Core has terminal.put and file/exec primitives; complete retained upload/download/overwrite/cancel behavior was not exercised.
gaps.required_evidence: Route-specific binary and safety scenarios A25–A26.
gaps.forbidden_workaround: Treating text file methods as full transfer parity or installing a new host file service.

gaps.title: Core machine actions with exact target identity
gaps.issue: Core machine.list and mutation results expose a permanent machine ID, but machine.connect, machine.rename and machine.rm accept only the mutable local name. A selected name can be reassigned to another Core before an action arrives, so the current RPCs cannot guarantee that a GUI action reaches the selected machine.
gaps.required_evidence: A Core-owned ID target or atomic expected-ID guard on connect, rename and remove; schema/client updates and a private concurrent rename/name-reuse test that refuses a changed target without acting on another machine; then GUI A04.
gaps.forbidden_workaround: Treating a preflight machine.list or post-action ID comparison as atomic, silently acting by name, or routing the action through legacy SSH/Herdr 1 state.

gaps.title: Read-only terminal link target without plugin activation
gaps.issue: The Herdr 1 pane.link.activate call can run a plugin handler but also returns the full URL of a wrapped link. pane.link.resolve returns only cell spans, the local surface lacks a soft-wrap flag, and pinned Core 0.1.18 advertises no read-only link target route.
gaps.required_evidence: A verified side-effect-free typed link target/span for exact terminal identity, content revision and viewport/cell, or equivalent proven terminal surface semantics; then negative plugin-activation and retained wrapped URL/file/chat/native interaction scenarios A30/A33.
gaps.forbidden_workaround: Keep plugin-capable activation for some clicks, guess a wrapped URL from adjacent painted rows, or disable wrapped links while claiming retained UX.

gaps.title: Authoritative usage/automation visibility
gaps.issue: Current Sheprd visibility depends in part on its own provider probes and automation daemon, both excluded. No equivalent complete Core feed is established.
gaps.required_evidence: Supported source contract and A20 without removed collectors/schedulers; document the exact coverage.
gaps.forbidden_workaround: Retain a hidden scheduler/provider login, scrape secrets or present unavailable values as zero/empty.

gaps.title: Production identity/signing/update ownership
gaps.issue: D61/D64 macOS preview identity ai.2389.spaceport, 2389 signing and tagged signed/notarized arm64 previews are validated. D65 selects Sparkle with Spaceport-owned keys and a signed preview feed; source checks, signed-feed rejection/selection and GUI/daemon lifecycle components pass. Native install/relaunch is blocked by a locked desktop, and the updated protected release/feed workflow still needs qualification. General-production and other-platform identities, package update routes and complete installation/native isolation remain open. D60 keeps the inherited custom updater removed.
gaps.required_evidence: Owner-controlled values plus A42–A44; publishing separately authorized.
gaps.forbidden_workaround: Inherit upstream signing identities/endpoints, claim domain ownership or ship development placeholders.

gaps.title: Native platform and full application verification
gaps.issue: Spaceport binaries have compiled and passed unit, protocol/component, executable CLI and macOS signed-package checks; earlier isolated native UI fixtures exposed activation failures. Complete native A49–A51 acceptance, final-preview GUI and real-agent/remote chat parity remain unproved. Package/component success is not full desktop acceptance.
gaps.required_evidence: Pinned source/schema plus native A49–A51 and all mandatory applicable scenarios.
gaps.forbidden_workaround: Claiming compilation/spec validation equals desktop or tailnet runtime support.
